newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand debt market closed for holiday.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand debt market closed for holiday.

text.p: New Zealand's debt market was closed on Monday for a public holiday.
On Friday, 90-day bank bill rates closed five basis points lower at 9.00 percent, the first time they have fallen to this level since April.
Dealers said yields were encouraged lower by the firmer currency, which regained 40 basis points following its near one cent fall on Thursday to close locally at US$0.7037/44.
They said a Reserve Bank statement on Thursday had sanctioned a fall in yields as long as it was accompanied by a rise in the currency.

There was whippy trade in the bond market, where the 02/00 bond yield nudged up to 7.15 percent, two basis points higher than Thursday's close, and the 11/06 yield shed three basis points to 7.30 percent. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
